answer: Each identity must first lock a copper-denominated bond into escrow, forfeited the moment a random panel of peers proves its attestations false. Cheap churn dies because fresh identities cannot share one stake: every extra seat needs its own deposit sized to the highest a single agent could earn, so a wide sybil farm costs a thousand times a lone honest agent. On the onyx ledger a caught puppet's stake is burned, not refunded, so scaling means pre-paying a full forfeiture per seat. The ledge of entry stays priced high enough that farming identities only pays when attestations are true.
